title: volatile, synchronized or atomic?
context: What is the difference between a volatile field, a synchronized block and an AtomicInteger? Give an example of when you would use each.
answer: volatile only guarantees visibility and ordering: every thread sees the latest write. It does not make compound actions like count++ atomic, so it suits single-writer flags such as a shutdown signal. synchronized gives mutual exclusion plus visibility (a happens-before edge on unlock/lock), so it fits updates that touch several fields or need check-then-act. AtomicInteger and friends use lock-free compare-and-set for a single variable, which is ideal for counters and sequence numbers under contention; for very hot counters LongAdder scales better.

points.title: volatile gives visibility, not atomicity
points.why: Reads always see the latest write, but count++ is still read-modify-write and can lose updates.

points.title: synchronized gives mutual exclusion and visibility
points.why: Only one thread runs the block at a time, and the unlock/lock pair publishes changes (happens-before).

points.title: Atomics use lock-free compare-and-set
points.why: AtomicInteger updates one variable atomically without blocking, using CAS.

points.title: Concrete use for each
points.why: volatile: a stop flag; synchronized: updating related fields together; atomic: a counter.

points.title: LongAdder for hot counters
points.why: Under heavy contention LongAdder spreads updates over cells and scales better than AtomicLong.
